title: Knight+Rook VS Queen
summary: Use checks to gain time against a promotion, and let the new queen obstruct its own king in the final mating net.

nodes.question: How can White create time before ...f1=Q?
nodes.explanation: A direct Re1 permits ...fxe1=Q. White first restricts the black king with h5, then uses checks to redirect the rook or construct mate.

branches.title: Allow the queen, then use it as a blocker
commentary: The f2 pawn is about to promote. Look for forcing threats against the king before trying to stop the pawn directly.
h5+ checks the king on g6. Black must answer the pawn check before considering promotion; the only legal replies are Kf6, Kh6 and Kxh5.
Kh6 keeps the h-pawn alive and avoids the immediate Rf7 mate seen after ...Kf6.
Nf7+ checks h6 and makes Black address the king’s safety before promoting.
Kxh5 accepts the pawn. With the knight now on f7, White cannot use the earlier Rh7+ route.
Re5+ uses the rook to check along the fifth rank instead.
Kh4 heads down the board. This is the source’s selected defensive continuation.
Ng5 is a quiet move: the knight supports a different checking route and prepares Nf3+ after promotion.
f1=Q promotes with check up the f-file toward Kf4.
Nf3+ interposes on the f-file and checks h4 at the same time. White meets a check with a check.
Kh3 escapes the knight check, but the king remains vulnerable to the rook.
Rh5+ checks down the h-file, supported by the knight on f3.
Kg2 walks onto the queen’s diagonal. Black’s own queen still occupies f1.
Rh2# checks across the second rank. Nf3 protects the rook and covers g1 and h4; Kf4 covers f3 and g3. Black’s queen blocks f1 and cannot capture the rook or interpose on g2-h2.

branches.title: The king chooses the wrong side
commentary: The first king reply already reveals why White spends a tempo on h5.
h5+ gives check and forces a king response. The pawn also controls g6, helping to restrict Black’s retreat.
Kf6 steps onto a square where the white king and knight remove the available flights.
Rf7# checks along the f-file. Nd8 protects f7 and covers e6; Kf4 covers e5, f5 and g5. The rook covers the seventh rank and the h5 pawn covers g6.

branches.title: Capture the pawn before the knight moves
commentary: If Black captures the h-pawn immediately, White’s rook can reach the first rank with tempo.
h5+ checks and offers the pawn to pull Black’s king onto the h-file.
Kxh5 accepts while White’s knight is still on d8.
Rh7+ forces a king response and puts the rook on the file it needs.
Kg6 is the illustrated retreat. Black has spent a move answering check rather than promoting.
Rh1 controls f1 from the side, preparing to capture the promoted piece. White keeps a checked win; this selected line stops at the successful defensive setup.

exercises.prompt: Why does the timing of ...Kxh5 matter?
exercises.answer: Before Nf7+, White has Rh7+ followed by Rh1. After the knight reaches f7, the rook must instead check from e5 and build a mating net.

exercises.prompt: How can a new queen fail to save the king?
exercises.answer: Nf3+ blocks its f-file check with tempo. At the end the queen occupies f1, removing a flight square, while a contact rook check leaves no square to interpose.
